topic.title: Trajectory-Based Policy Optimization and Off-Policy Reuse
topic.overview: Continuous-control policies can be improved by optimizing trajectories, reparameterizing action distributions, or reusing earlier interaction data. This topic connects policy search with importance sampling, dynamics models, and expressive generative policies. A recurring concern is balancing exploration and low-variance updates while correcting the mismatch between collected data and the policy being learned.
topic.whyItMatters: New environment interactions can be expensive, yet careless reuse creates biased value estimates or unsupported actions. Good representations and distribution corrections can make past experience useful for new control objectives.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives study motion-controller optimization and guided policy search. Later work develops trajectory-based off-policy learning and coherent exploration. Recent methods extend optimization to multimodal or diffusion policies and investigate training-free adaptation through successor measures and stationary density ratios, linking reuse to zero-shot task changes.
openQuestions: When can a learned density correction be trusted outside well-covered actions?
How should expressive policies trade multimodality against stable optimization?
